title: Move baked cookies from a sheet pan to a cooling rack with a turner, without touching or breaking them
instruction: Move the four cookies from the sheet pan onto the cooling rack with the spatula, without touching or breaking them, then put the spatula back on its rest.
context: Lifting freshly baked cookies off a sheet pan onto a cooling rack with a spatula is one of the most familiar moments in a home kitchen, a school bake sale or a bakery; cookie-dough packages end their directions with it (cool briefly on the sheet, then remove). Anyone can judge the result at a glance: every cookie whole and flat on the rack, none broken, dropped or touched by hand. Nothing is turned over: the skill is getting a 0.6 mm blade under a brittle item, carrying it level, and setting it down on wire without a drop, for several items in a row, with no hand ever on the food.
setup: On the table, as in the screenshot (x forward from the robot, y to its left, from the midpoint between the arm bases; arms at y +0.305 and -0.305 m). (1) Aluminium quarter sheet pan, 330 x 241 mm rim, 305 x 216 mm flat floor, 25 mm deep, about 0.40 kg, bare (no liner), long side pointing away from the robot, centre at x 0.335, y -0.060; loose on the table. (2) Four cookies, 76 mm across, 10 mm thick and 35 g (the size and mass of a baked Otis Spunkmeyer Sweet Discovery Triple Chocolate cookie, item 58814), firm and brittle, the base's outer 6 mm curled up 1.5 mm; real trials use a non-perishable printed stand-in of the same size, mass and friction that parts in two halves when bent past the break limit (README, "Cookie stand-in"), its joint running along y, flat side down on the far two thirds of the pan with centres at (0.335, -0.115), (0.335, -0.005), (0.440, -0.115) and (0.440, -0.005). (3) Wire cooling rack, 305 x 216 mm, 17 mm high, 2 mm wires 10 mm apart running away from the robot, about 0.22 kg, loose, right of the pan with centre at x 0.360, y -0.330. (4) Offset turner (cookie spatula): stainless blade 90 x 65 mm, 0.6 mm thick, 30 mm below a 110 x 22 x 14 mm plastic handle, about 69 g, lying on a rest fixed to the table (two posts 32 mm high under the handle, a pad under the blade) with the handle's middle at x 0.280, y -0.600, blade pointing away from the robot. Both arms start raised in the ready pose.
scoring: Count at the end, from a photo plus the trial video. Each cookie is one of: GOOD (+0.2): lying flat (within 8 degrees) with its whole outline on the rack's wires, not on another cookie or on the turner, at rest, in one piece, never touched by a gripper or any other part of the robot, and never dropped. SPOILED (-0.1): broken at any time (a stand-in's two halves parted); or touched by any part of the robot at any time; or dropped (a free fall of about 18 mm or more, 0.6 m/s downward in simulation); or ending anywhere other than the pan or the rack (table, floor, turner, hanging on a rim). LEFT (0): still on the pan in one piece and untouched, or on the rack but overhanging its frame, leaning or stacked. Score = 0.2 x GOOD - 0.1 x SPOILED, never below 0, so four good cookies give 0.8. The last 0.2 is given only when all four are GOOD and, for at least 1 second, the pan is where it started (centre within 30 mm, turned no more than 10 degrees, flat on the table), the turner is back on its rest (handle middle within 15 mm of its starting place, pointing within 15 degrees, lying on the posts), both grippers are at least 80 mm from the pan, the rack and the turner, and nothing is moving. The whole trial scores 0 if the pan is ever tipped more than 10 degrees or lifted more than 20 mm off the table (a hot pan must not be poured from). Doing nothing scores 0. Measure with a ruler against tape marks made at setup (pan outline, rest), a count of whole and parted stand-ins, and the video for touches and drops.
reset_notes: Real trials use the printed cookie stand-ins (README, "Cookie stand-in"), made once and reused, each passing the acceptance checks (34 to 36 g; 76 mm across, 10 mm thick; holds 1.6 N and parts by 2.45 N in a 40 mm three-point bend; tilt-slide 33 to 37 degrees on the pan, 12 to 16 on the turner, 24.5 to 28.5 on the rack). Press any parted stand-in back together from its own two halves; re-check one dropped on the floor. Set four flat side down on the bare, dry trial pan at the marked places, joint along y. Put the pan and rack back on their tape marks and the turner on its rest, blade away from the robot.
fidelity: True-size rigid bodies in PhysX with real contact; the 0.6 mm blade is a collider. A cookie is one rigid body that breaks by a criterion on measured contact forces (0.02 N m bending, 3 N squeeze, 10 N press); it cannot crumble or bend. Its base edge curls up 1.5 mm, which lets the blade in. Friction is fixed (cookie on pan 0.7, on blade 0.25; real stand-ins are tested to these); cookies do not stick, the pan is not hot, the blade does not flex. The pan stays put, so one arm does the job.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, ended at the 2,400-step limit); scripted demo: 1.0 in 1,872 steps. Both on this task file (SHA-256 prefix 5bec6a6dc68e).
